source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
The Franklin campus publishes 6 MW of IT capacity across 80,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 6 MW supports roughly 150 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical enterprise colocation density, it supports roughly 600 racks. The operator has not published power density targets, so which figure applies is unknown. Six megawatts is a modest footprint by hyperscale standards, placing this campus in the range where a single large AI training cluster would fill it entirely.

The certification stack, SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 for audit controls, PCI DSS for payment card environments, HIPAA and HITRUST for protected health information, ISO 27001 for information security management, and SSAE 18 as the attestation standard underlying the SOC reports, collectively qualify the facility to host regulated workloads in financial services and healthcare. These certifications are compliance prerequisites, not performance indicators, and say nothing about the tenants actually present.

Among the 24 facilities this site has mapped in Tennessee, only one, this campus, has a published IT capacity figure, so the state total of 6 MW reflects this single site and not the state's true installed base. That gap means the campus ranks first in Tennessee by published MW, but that ranking is an artifact of incomplete data rather than evidence of scale leadership. Tennessee's broader data center footprint remains largely unquantified on published operator spec pages.
